subject: Physics
title: Grade 9 Olympiad Physics Core 1B Phenomenological Reconstruction: Motion in a Plane

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Simultaneous Dropped vs Horizontally Projected Sphere Impact
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: y = (1/2) g t^2 => t = sqrt(2h/g) for both; horizontal velocity u_x = u has zero projection onto y-axis.
reconstruction_cycles.phenomenological_reconstruction: Reconstruct from Galilean relativity. Suppose you drop a ball inside a train moving at constant speed u. In your frame, it falls vertically in time sqrt(2h/g). To a platform observer, the ball follows a parabolic arc with horizontal range u sqrt(2h/g). Because the laws of mechanics are identical in both frames, the flight time cannot depend on train velocity.

limiting_boundary_checks.expected_outcome: Reduces to 1D vertical drop from height h: t = sqrt(2h/g), x = 0
Fall time remains strictly sqrt(2h/g); landing range scales to infinity: x -> infinity

reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: R(theta) = u^2 sin(2 theta) / g. Since sin(2(90 - theta)) = sin(180 - 2 theta) = sin(2 theta), R(theta) = R(90 - theta). Flight time T = 2u sin theta / g; ratio of flight times T_1 / T_2 = tan theta.
reconstruction_cycles.phenomenological_reconstruction: A shallow launch (e.g. 30 degrees) has high horizontal speed but spends brief time in the air. A steep launch (60 degrees) spends prolonged time aloft but advances horizontally at sluggish pace. At complementary angles, the trade-off balances with mathematical precision: (Fast speed x Short time) equals (Slow speed x Long time).

limiting_boundary_checks.expected_outcome: sin(2 * 45) = sin(90) = 1 => Maximum possible range R_max = u^2 / g
sin(180) = 0 => Range R = 0; vertical height H = u^2 / (2g)

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: River-Boat Shortest Time vs Zero Drift
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Crossing time t = d / (v_bw cos theta). Minimum time t_min = d / v_bw at theta = 0. Zero drift requires v_bw sin theta = v_w => sin theta = v_w / v_bw with crossing time t = d / sqrt(v_bw^2 - v_w^2).
reconstruction_cycles.phenomenological_reconstruction: Separate across-river travel from along-river drift. The river current pushes only downstream; it has zero capability to transport the boat across the river. To get across as quickly as possible, 100% of boat propulsion must point directly across. Angling upstream wastes engine power fighting downstream drift rather than crossing.

limiting_boundary_checks.expected_outcome: Zero-drift and minimum-time paths become identical: theta = 0, t = d / v_bw
Zero drift requires theta = 90 degrees; crossing time t -> infinity (boat hovers stationary)

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Relative Rain Velocity & Forward Umbrella Tilt
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: v_{rel} = v_{rain} - v_{runner} = -v_r j_hat - v_m i_hat. Relative angle from vertical is tan phi = v_m / v_r. Umbrella tilt is forward at angle phi.
reconstruction_cycles.phenomenological_reconstruction: To understand relative motion, bring the runner to rest by adding equal and opposite velocity -v_m to everything. Rain now possesses downward speed v_r and horizontal headwind speed v_m blowing directly into the runner's face. The resultant vector slants from the front, requiring the umbrella to tilt forward.

limiting_boundary_checks.expected_outcome: tan phi = 0 => phi = 0; umbrella held vertical
tan phi -> infinity => phi -> 90 degrees; rain appears horizontal

cognitive_dissonance_probes.scenario: A cannon on a flat horizontal plain fires a shell at 30 degrees with initial speed 100 m/s. An identical shell is fired at 60 degrees with the same 100 m/s speed.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.dissonance_question: Which shell lands farther away? Which shell stays in the air longer?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: Both shells land at the exact same distance (R = 866 m, since 30 and 60 degrees are complementary). However, the 60-degree shell spends sqrt(3) times longer in the air (T_60 = 17.3 s vs T_30 = 10.0 s) and reaches three times the maximum height.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.scenario: A boat can travel at 5 m/s in still water. It crosses a 100 m wide river flowing at 3 m/s.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.dissonance_question: What is the shortest possible time to reach the opposite bank? Does downstream drift increase this time?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: The shortest crossing time is exactly 20.0 seconds (t = 100 m / 5 m/s). Downstream drift has zero impact on crossing time because river flow is strictly orthogonal to the crossing direction.
